chapter: Les Hite, Sebastian's and Duke Ellington
title: Louis Armstrong at Sebastian's Cotton Club
summary: Royal heard Armstrong on Fletcher Henderson records, played the clarinet parts when Louis fronted the Hite band, and shared manager Joe Glaser later.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Okay. When Louie Armstrong came to Sebastian's Cotton Club, had you heard him before on records? That was his first trip to the West Coast, wasn't it?

That was his first trip. Everybody had heard Louie Armstrong that was interested in jazz because the first time I heard Louie Armstrong, actually was with the old, old Fletcher Henderson records, when I was just a little kid.

He had, Fletcher Henderson had those big bands at the time. One of the first black bands that ever played together written arrangements and he had some fine people. He had Coleman Hawkins and Louis Armstrong and all those people playing, you know? And everybody knew Louis, but I'd never worked with him.

Actually, the first time I worked with Louis, I had the misfortune to have to lay off and so he came in town with a -- and brought some of his arrangements with him from back East and he had some tunes in there like "High Society," that had famous clarinet solos in it and there's nobody around town that could play the clarinet solos to "High Society." So, they made sure that they had me playing in the band out there when Louis was there, so I could play all the clarinet parts.

So, that was a nice experience, playing with Louis. He's a fine man, very fine man. So, maybe that's one of the reasons why Les Hite sent for me in the first place, because he knew that Louis was going to be coming and needing a clarinet player. So, that's --
Did you ever work with him again after that?

No, not really, as a part of his band. The only time I ever worked with him was with the Les Hite Band out at the old Sebastian's Cotton Club, because after that, he had his own groups and he went his way and I went another way. The closest I ever got to him was, I worked under

the same manager, Joe Glazer, (PHONETIC) worked with Lionel Hampton as Louis Armstrong did, because he was under Joe Glazer also. So, we would cross paths quite often and we turned out to be excellent friends and we always had a mutual admiration society between he and I because he was such a fine guy and very comical and always had something going. Just a great man.
